history.dynasty: Vengi Chalukyas (Kubja Vishnu Vardhana) per Wikipedia; Chola patronage (Krimikanta Chola, 5th-15th c. per local tradition — dates conflict); Gajapati and Vijayanagara kings; 1850 renovation by Diwan Sri Raja Kadrengula Jogi Jagannatha Rao and Raja Vasireddi Venkatadri Nayudu
history.period: Ancient (origins disputed: 5th c. CE Salivahana Saka 515 per local tradition; 15th c. CE per Wikipedia; centrally protected monument of national importance)
history.summary: The Bhavanarayana Temple at Bapatla is the temple that gave the town its name — one of the centrally protected monuments of national importance (ASI). Its origins are disputed: local tradition dates it to Salivahana Saka 515 (5th century CE) under Chola king Krimikanta Chola (also claimed 1265/1465 AD in some accounts), while Wikipedia's account attributes construction to the Vengi Chalukya ruler Kubja Vishnu Vardhana (7th century). The 75-ft rajagopuram is said to be built from a single rock, and inscriptions on the walls are in Telugu, Tamil and Sanskrit. It received patronage from the Gajapatis and Vijayanagara kings, and was renovated in 1850. NOTE: the CSV name 'Sri Bhavanaranya Swamy Temple' is a misspelling of Bhavanarayana, and the CSV town 'Guntur' is wrong — the temple is in Bapatla town, formerly of Guntur district and now of Bapatla district. A second Bhavanarayana temple exists at Sarpavaram near Kakinada (Kakinada district), which is a different, famous shrine — the Guntur-district context of this CSV row points to Bapatla, but the intended referent should be confirmed.

name: Sri Bhavanaranya Swamy Temple
town_description: Bapatla is a coastal town in Bapatla district, Andhra Pradesh (formerly part of Guntur district), roughly 70 km south of Guntur city. The town takes its name from the Bhavanarayana temple, and it is also known for the Suryalanka beach nearby and as a cashew and agriculture trading centre (verify).

travel.airport: Nearest functional airport is Vijayawada (Gannavaram), roughly 100 km away (verify).
travel.railway: Bapatla railway station serves the town, with services from Vijayawada, Chennai and Hyderabad (verify timings and station details).
travel.road: Well connected by road; about 70 km south of Guntur and ~100 km from Vijayawada (verify distances).

visitor_information.best_time: October to February for pleasant coastal weather. The annual Brahmotsavam / Chariot Festival is the biggest occasion but very crowded.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Reported 6:00 AM to 8:00 PM, all days (verify on site).
